<main class="site-main"><section class="page-intro"><p class="section-number">Experiment · Python toolkit</p><h1>Local Agent Toolkit</h1><div class="article-meta"><span class="status">in bloom</span><span>updated 02 Jul 2026</span></div><p>How small can a local worker be before it stops being useful?</p></section><article class="prose"><p>Local Agent Toolkit lets a developer delegate bounded tasks to a local Ollama model: repository exploration, first-pass review, test ideas, diagnostics, and candidate patches.</p><h2>Question</h2><p>Can local compute handle the narrow, repetitive parts of engineering work while a human remains the authority?</p><h2>Design</h2><p>The toolkit filters repository context, blocks sensitive paths by default, and treats the local model's output as untrusted advice. Most commands are read-only. Candidate patches print diffs instead of applying them.</p><h2>Limitation</h2><p>Token savings depend on the task, model, context size, and verification overhead. A bounded interface enables control; it does not guarantee a fixed reduction.</p><p><a class="text-link" href="https://github.com/tomerzipori/local-agent-toolkit">Open the repository</a></p></article></main>
